motivation: Added GO-eligible pairs have similarly lower mean conservation in native high and medium evidence strata. Identify whether these relations arise within retained HMM-supported seed components or across satellite-expanded seed boundaries before choosing another accuracy mechanism.
inputs: Admitted matched control and component native results; original checkpoint gene order; original broad graph partition; reproduced control and component refined seeds; final component candidate partition; executed large-copy trace; immutable HMM-derived graph arrays; retained GO/EC raw eligible pair scores.
operation: Describe shared, added and removed GO/EC-eligible pairs by original-family co-membership, component-seed co-membership, bounded-retention activation, expanded-candidate co-membership and direct HMM-derived graph support (absent, positive below 1.5, at least 1.5). Reproduce admitted raw counts and means. Use chunked, read-only NumPy .npy access and checked integer indexing; preserve both gene universe and source order.
selection: Use structure to distinguish candidate-boundary from reconciliation hypotheses. Do not change inference, filter pairs by reference annotation, choose score cutoffs from GO/EC values or claim that functional conservation proves orthology.
limitations: This is development-exposed descriptive localization, not independent confirmation or causal attribution.
Direct HMM-derived graph support is homology evidence, not proof of orthology.
No native inference, rescoring, default promotion or uncertainty estimation.
